🐞 Bugs (2) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Ack doesn’t clear badge 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>UpdateNotification.acknowledgeEpisodes() updates localStorage but does not bump
>episodeNoticeRevision, so episodeNotices (and thus notificationCount/showBadge) can stay cached and
>continue showing unread episode notifications after “Mark all as read” or closing the panel.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[R95-104]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/pull/44/files#diff-a96b7ea30a4c68e25f4975bcc09922896c2e7d7f8810df7188b0c5afedcc130aR95-R104) > >```diff > function acknowledgeEpisodes() { > for (const notice of episodeNotices.value) { >- localStorage.setItem(`miku-episode-notice-${notice.id}`, String(notice.episode)) >+ localStorage.setItem(`miku-episode-notice-${authStore.currentUser?.id}-${notice.id}`, String(notice.episode)) > } >- showBadge.value = hasUpdate.value && !wasDismissedForCurrent() > } > > function markAllAsRead() { > acknowledgeEpisodes() > if (hasUpdate.value) dismissUpdate() >- showBadge.value = false > } >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>episodeNotices is intentionally tied to episodeNoticeRevision for cache invalidation, but
>acknowledgeEpisodes does not update that revision. Since the unread filter depends on localStorage
>reads, Vue won’t recompute episodeNotices after localStorage writes, leaving
>notificationCount/showBadge stale.
>
> > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[26-58]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/4a7c01d50cca46c459ad44e4065f73725aa144e0/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L26-L58) > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[95-111]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/4a7c01d50cca46c459ad44e4065f73725aa144e0/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L95-L111) >
>

> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >`episodeNotices` is a computed value that is manually invalidated via `episodeNoticeRevision`. The PR’s new computed badge/count relies on `episodeNotices`, but `acknowledgeEpisodes()` only writes to `localStorage` (non-reactive) and never increments `episodeNoticeRevision`, so the badge/count can remain stale after acknowledging. > >### Issue Context >- `episodeNotices` reads `episodeNoticeRevision.value` to create a reactive dependency, and filters by values read from `localStorage`. >- `acknowledgeEpisodes()` writes the seen values to `localStorage`, but does not change any reactive dependency. > >### Fix Focus Areas >- frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[26-58] >- frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[95-116] > >### Suggested fix >- Increment `episodeNoticeRevision.value++` at the end of `acknowledgeEpisodes()` (and/or in `markAllAsRead()` after calling it) so the computed re-runs and the badge/count reflect the newly stored "seen" values. >- Alternatively, replace the manual revision invalidation with a reactive in-memory “seen” map that you update alongside localStorage. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Hiatus/cancelled notices suppressed 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>releasedEpisode is now only set for RELEASING items with nextAiringEpisode or FINISHED items, so
>entries in statuses like HIATUS/CANCELLED (or RELEASING without nextAiringEpisode) produce `episode:
>undefined` and are always filtered out, potentially hiding valid “new episode / you’re behind”
>notices.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[R36-41]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/pull/44/files#diff-a96b7ea30a4c68e25f4975bcc09922896c2e7d7f8810df7188b0c5afedcc130aR36-R41) > >```diff >+ let releasedEpisode: number | undefined >+ if (media?.status === 'RELEASING' && media.nextAiringEpisode) { >+ releasedEpisode = media.nextAiringEpisode.episode - 1 >+ } else if (media?.status === 'FINISHED') { >+ releasedEpisode = media.episodes >+ } >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The component now leaves releasedEpisode undefined for statuses other than (RELEASING with
>nextAiringEpisode) and FINISHED, and then filters out notices with falsy/undefined episode values.
>The codebase defines additional valid statuses (HIATUS/CANCELLED), so those statuses will never
>generate episode notices under the new logic.
>
> > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[26-54]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/4a7c01d50cca46c459ad44e4065f73725aa144e0/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L26-L54) > [frontend/src/types/index.ts[46-53]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/4a7c01d50cca46c459ad44e4065f73725aa144e0/frontend/src/types/index.ts/#L46-L53) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >`releasedEpisode` is only computed for `RELEASING` (when `nextAiringEpisode` exists) and `FINISHED`. For other AniList statuses (e.g., `HIATUS`, `CANCELLED`), `releasedEpisode` remains `undefined`, and the subsequent filter drops the notice entirely. > >### Issue Context >The repo’s `MediaStatus` type includes `HIATUS` and `CANCELLED`, so these cases are expected to exist in real data. > >### Fix Focus Areas >- frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[26-54] >- frontend/src/types/index.ts[46-53] > >### Suggested fix >- Decide which additional statuses should still use a released-episode boundary (commonly `HIATUS` and possibly `CANCELLED`), and set `releasedEpisode = media.episodes` for those. >- Keep excluding `NOT_YET_RELEASED` to avoid planned totals being treated as released episodes. >- Optionally add a guarded fallback for `RELEASING` when `nextAiringEpisode` is missing (only if you can ensure `media.episodes` represents aired episodes in that scenario). >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

issue.title: issue raised by qodo
issue.body:
Code Review by Qodo

🐞 Bugs (4) 📘 Rule violations (0) 📜 Skill insights (0)
1. Badge ignores episode notices 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>In UpdateNotification.vue, the hasUpdate watcher sets showBadge=false whenever no update is
>available, even if episodeNotices still exist (and useUpdate is a shared singleton affected by the
>Settings “Check for Updates” action). Also, the hasEpisodeNotice watcher never clears showBadge when
>notices disappear, which can leave a visible badge showing "0".
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[R68-78]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/pull/40/files#diff-a96b7ea30a4c68e25f4975bcc09922896c2e7d7f8810df7188b0c5afedcc130aR68-R78) > >```diff > watch(hasUpdate, (available) => { >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The hasUpdate watcher unconditionally clears showBadge when updates are unavailable, while the
>episode watcher only ever sets it to true; because useUpdate’s refs are module-scoped, ProfileView’s
>manual update check can flip hasUpdate and trigger this clearing even when episode notices remain.
>
> > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[68-78]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L68-L78) > [frontend/src/composables/useUpdate.ts[28-43]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/composables/useUpdate.ts/#L28-L43) > [frontend/src/views/ProfileView.vue[115-139]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/views/ProfileView.vue/#L115-L139) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >`showBadge` is managed by separate watchers and can become inconsistent: update checks can clear the badge while episode notices still exist, and episode notices going away can leave a stale badge (even showing `0`). > >### Issue Context >`useUpdate()` is implemented with module-level refs, so update checks from other views (e.g. Settings/ProfileView) mutate the same `hasUpdate` ref watched by the notification bell. > >### Fix Focus Areas >- frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[68-116] >- frontend/src/composables/useUpdate.ts[28-43] >- frontend/src/views/ProfileView.vue[115-139] > >### Implementation notes >- Prefer making `showBadge` a computed derived from `(hasUpdate && !wasDismissedForCurrent()) || hasEpisodeNotice`. >- If you keep `showBadge` as a ref, update it in a single place (e.g., a watcher on `[hasUpdate, hasEpisodeNotice]`) and ensure it is set both true and false appropriately. >- Ensure the badge count and visibility never result in a visible `0` badge. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
2. Notices persist after logout 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>The bell’s episodeNotices computation reads animeStore.myList regardless of auth state, and the auth
>watcher only fetches on login without clearing anything on logout. Since authStore.logout() doesn’t
>clear animeStore.myList, users can see the previous account’s episode notifications after signing
>out.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[R80-84]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/pull/40/files#diff-a96b7ea30a4c68e25f4975bcc09922896c2e7d7f8810df7188b0c5afedcc130aR80-R84) > >```diff >+watch(() => authStore.isLoggedIn, async (loggedIn) => { >+ if (loggedIn && authStore.currentUser) { >+ await animeStore.fetchMyList(authStore.currentUser.id) >+ } >+}) >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>UpdateNotification derives notices from animeStore.myList and only fetches on login; on logout,
>authStore clears user/isAuthenticated but animeStore.myList remains populated because it’s only
>assigned during fetchMyList and never cleared, so the component can continue to render previous-user
>notices.
>
> > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[25-48]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L25-L48) > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[80-84]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L80-L84) > [frontend/src/stores/auth.ts[171-187]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/stores/auth.ts/#L171-L187) > [frontend/src/stores/anime.ts[253-257]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/stores/anime.ts/#L253-L257) > [frontend/src/stores/anime.ts[302-318]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/stores/anime.ts/#L302-L318) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >### Issue description >Episode notifications can remain visible after logout because `animeStore.myList` is cached and not cleared when auth state changes to logged-out. > >### Issue Context >- `episodeNotices` derives from `animeStore.myList`. >- `authStore.logout()` clears auth state only. >- `animeStore.fetchMyList()` assigns `myList`, but there is no corresponding clear on logout. > >### Fix Focus Areas >- frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[25-48] >- frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[80-84] >- frontend/src/stores/auth.ts[171-188] >- frontend/src/stores/anime.ts[253-257] >- frontend/src/stores/anime.ts[302-318] > >### Implementation notes >- Add an explicit `clearMyList()` (and possibly `clearAnimeState()`) action on the anime store that sets `myList.value = null`. >- Call that clear action on logout (e.g., in logout handlers like ProfileView/MyListView) and/or in the auth watcher when `loggedIn` becomes false. >- Additionally, guard `episodeNotices` to return `[]` when `!authStore.isLoggedIn` to avoid rendering cached data. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Planned episodes trigger notices 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>episodeNotices uses media.episodes as the "released" episode count for any non-RELEASING status, so
>NOT_YET_RELEASED/HIATUS/CANCELLED entries can generate false "new episode" notifications based on
>planned totals rather than actually released episodes.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[R33-36]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/pull/40/files#diff-a96b7ea30a4c68e25f4975bcc09922896c2e7d7f8810df7188b0c5afedcc130aR33-R36) > >```diff >+ const releasedEpisode = media?.status === 'RELEASING' && media.nextAiringEpisode >+ ? media.nextAiringEpisode.episode - 1 >+ : media?.episodes >+ return { >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The code falls back to media.episodes for non-RELEASING statuses; the project’s own MediaStatus
>type includes NOT_YET_RELEASED/HIATUS/CANCELLED, where episodes can be planned rather than

1. Badge ignores episode notices 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>In UpdateNotification.vue, the hasUpdate watcher sets showBadge=false whenever no update is
>available, even if episodeNotices still exist (and useUpdate is a shared singleton affected by the
>Settings “Check for Updates” action). Also, the hasEpisodeNotice watcher never clears showBadge when
>notices disappear, which can leave a visible badge showing "0".
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[R68-78]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/pull/40/files#diff-a96b7ea30a4c68e25f4975bcc09922896c2e7d7f8810df7188b0c5afedcc130aR68-R78) > >```diff > watch(hasUpdate, (available) => { >``` >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The hasUpdate watcher unconditionally clears showBadge when updates are unavailable, while the
>episode watcher only ever sets it to true; because useUpdate’s refs are module-scoped, ProfileView’s
>manual update check can flip hasUpdate and trigger this clearing even when episode notices remain.
>
> > [frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue[68-78]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/components/layout/UpdateNotification.vue/#L68-L78) > [frontend/src/composables/useUpdate.ts[28-43]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/composables/useUpdate.ts/#L28-L43) > [frontend/src/views/ProfileView.vue[115-139]](https://github.com/Aswanidev-vs/Miku/blob/f1779bdc3c56a66365ee36344fb0ab2774e21b07/frontend/src/views/ProfileView.vue/#L115-L139) >

> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. 2. Notices persist after logout 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>The bell’s episodeNotices computation reads animeStore.myList regardless of auth state, and the auth
>watcher only fetches on login without clearing anything on logout. Since authStore.logout() doesn’t
>clear animeStore.myList, users can see the previous account’s episode notifications after signing
